title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## PSA-PPO: Sim-to-Real Lettuce Harvesting

### The Breakthrough
The paper presents PSA‑PPO, a proximal‑policy‑optimization algorithm that adds target‑conditioned observations and corridor‑aware safety constraints for lettuce harvesting. By preserving the standard PPO objective while integrating spatial corridor constraints and trajectory‑history safety encoding, the method achieved 94.7 % reaching success on a real‑world UR10e arm, outperforming classical planners and reducing motion jerk by up to 39.8 %.

### The Caveats
The study provides no comparison to other reinforcement‑learning baselines nor any statistical variance reporting, so it’s unclear whether PSA‑PPO truly outperforms existing RL methods beyond the selected classical planners.

## Spark-0 Tactile Pretraining

### The Breakthrough
The authors release Spark‑0, a vision‑tactile‑language‑action model pretrained on a 1,000‑hour HumanTouch dataset that aligns visual tokens with contact maps and encodes regional force histories. This multimodal pretraining lets a single model run vision‑only or tactile‑conditioned policies, yielding substantial performance gains on dexterous manipulation tasks on a real robot compared to vision‑only baselines.

### The Caveats
The reported state‑of‑the‑art gains are demonstrated on only a single dexterous robot, so it remains unclear whether Spark‑0’s tactile pretraining generalizes to other hardware platforms.

## Value as Memory (VaM) Post‑training

### The Breakthrough
The Value as Memory (VaM) framework augments generalist robot policies with a short‑term value‑caching memory and an online RL schedule that blends offline demos, off‑policy corrections, and on‑policy rollouts. Empirically, value caching lifts success rates by 29.4 % and the online learning adds a further 32.8 % gain while running eight times more iterations at double the speed per gradient step.

### The Caveats
The paper reports large gains but provides no comparison to any existing baselines, so it’s unclear whether the improvements stem from the value‑caching scheme or merely from extra data or training time.

## LIBERO‑PeRM Benchmark

### The Breakthrough
The LIBERO‑PeRM benchmark isolates preference satisfaction from task completion by providing 312 paired demonstrations across five suites, each annotated with motion, skill, and user‑profile preferences expressed in language. This enables systematic zero‑shot personalization and preference‑learning evaluation for manipulation policies.

### The Caveats
The study reports results only in simulation with no real‑world robot experiments, so it’s unclear whether the benchmark’s insights about personalized manipulation will hold on actual hardware.

## OpenReality 3D Reconstruction

### The Breakthrough
The OpenReality repository turns handheld phone video into a persistent 3D scene that AI agents can query via 41 Model‑Context‑Protocol tools, supporting measurement, path planning, and robot‑training exports. It builds reconstruction on the VGGT‑SLAM library and offers an offline simulator for development without GPU or cloud resources.

### The Caveats
The repo offers no quantitative evaluation or comparison to existing SLAM/reconstruction systems, so its claimed general‑purpose accuracy and usefulness remain unverified.

## Claude Code Team Review Automation

### The Breakthrough
The Claude Code team moved most code‑review work to AI agents that run before a pull request exists, using Claude to run tests, builds, and screenshots, and flag bugs, style, or security issues. A risk‑tier classifier routes only high‑risk changes to humans, resulting in merged PRs more than doubling and substantive human comments rising from 16 % to 54 % of PRs.

### The Caveats
The reported improvements rely solely on internal metrics with no external or third‑party benchmark, so it’s unclear whether the approach would generalize beyond Anthropic’s own codebases.

### Priority
PSA‑PPO demonstrates that a modest augmentation to PPO can deliver near‑perfect real‑world harvesting performance without any fine‑tuning, making it the most actionable breakthrough for today’s robotics practitioners.

### One action
Try reproducing PSA‑PPO’s corridor‑aware safety constraints on your own manipulation tasks, starting with the provided Isaac Lab code.

### What to watch
Across the manipulation landscape, Spark‑0 shows how large‑scale tactile pretraining can boost dexterous control, VaM illustrates the value of online memory‑augmented fine‑tuning for generalist policies, and LIBERO‑PeRM provides a simulation benchmark to evaluate personalized behavior. Together they highlight a trend toward richer sensory inputs, continual adaptation, and user‑centric evaluation.
